questions.question: After a trip, what should you do?

options.text: Place the vehicle out of service.
Complete an after-trip inspection of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Complete an after-trip inspection of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: After each trip, you must inspect the vehicle you drove and file a report about it.

questions.question: To prevent liquid surge in tanks, you should:
questions.explanation: Liquid in tanks can surge and affect your driving. Start, slow down, and stop very smoothly to prevent this problem.

questions.question: After you finish a pre-trip inspection, what should you do?

options.text: Leave the rear shut-off valves open.
Leave the emergency line valve open.

questions.explanation: Before you drive, open the rear emergency line and service line shut-off valves to check that air reaches all brake systems. Then close both valves before you start driving.

questions.question: When a construction worker is near the road, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until construction is finished before driving.

questions.explanation: In construction zones, do not drive faster than the posted speed limit. Slow down even more when workers are near the road.

questions.question: About headlights, which is true?

options.text: They are usually not needed when driving at night.
They provide better light than the sun.
Use high beam whenever it is safe and legal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use high beam whenever it is safe and legal.
questions.explanation: Use high beam headlights at night when safe and legal to improve visibility. However, high beam light can blind other drivers. Switch to low beam when within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle.

questions.question: When driving, what should you do with your mirrors?

options.text: Do not use them because they distract you.
Use them only when there is other traffic.
Check them regularly only on cloudy days.

questions.explanation: You must know what is happening around you at all times. Check your mirrors regularly to stay aware of your surroundings.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, what should you do with engine belts?

options.text: Inspect them only if they look frayed.

questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check all engine belts for tightness and wear.

questions.question: When turning quickly to avoid an object in the road, what should you do?

options.text: Turn more than needed to have extra clearance.
Turn only as much as needed to miss the object.
Steer and accelerate at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only as much as needed to miss the object.
questions.explanation: When turning quickly to avoid an object, turn only enough to clear it. Do not use the brakes while turning.

questions.question: What is aggressive driving?

options.text: Driving in a selfish or pushy manner without regard for others
Driving with some care for other motorists' safety

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving in a selfish or pushy manner without regard for others
questions.explanation: Aggressive driving means operating a vehicle in a selfish or pushy way without regard for the safety of others.

questions.question: What are passive railroad crossings?

options.text: Crossings with no traffic control devices.
Crossings with gates that lower when trains approach.
Crossings that commercial vehicles should never use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossings with no traffic control devices.
questions.explanation: Passive railroad crossings have no traffic control devices. The driver must decide whether it is safe to cross the tracks.

questions.question: While driving, what should you do?

options.text: You do not need to tell others what you plan to do.
You should only use turn signals if another vehicle is next to you.
You should not use a turn signal if your lane change is obvious.
You should always use turn signals to tell others what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should always use turn signals to tell others what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always use proper turn signals. This tells other drivers on the road what you are about to do.

questions.question: What happens if a trailer is too high?

options.text: It will not make a difference when coupling.

questions.explanation: Before coupling a tractor and trailer, check the trailer height. If the trailer is too low, the nose may get damaged. If it is too high, it may not couple properly.

questions.question: Who must identify the hazard class of materials being shipped?
questions.explanation: The shipper is responsible for identifying the product ID number, shipping name, hazard class, packing group, and making sure the packaging, labels, marking, and placards are correct.

questions.question: If a tire fails, what should you do?

options.text: Loosen your grip on the steering wheel.
Check your tires after the vehicle stops completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your tires after the vehicle stops completely.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly if a tire fails. Do not use the brakes. Let the vehicle slow down on its own. When it slows enough, brake gently, pull off the road, and stop. Then check your tires.

questions.question: What is true about over-the-counter medication?

options.text: It poses no safety risks to drivers.
It is not mentioned in any driving under the influence laws.
It cannot affect a driver's abilities.
It can affect a person's ability to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can affect a person's ability to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Over-the-counter and prescription medications can have side effects that harm your driving ability. It is illegal to drive while under the influence of alcohol or drugs, including some over-the-counter medicines.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: It allows wheels to lock up.
It keeps wheels from locking up.
It makes it easier to turn a large vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It keeps wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops the wheels from locking up when you brake hard.

questions.question: When should you shift into a lower gear before going downhill?

options.text: As you go downhill and pick up speed.
Near the bottom of the hill.

questions.explanation: Always downshift before you start going downhill. Shifting into a lower gear at high speed can damage your transmission and reduce your ability to brake with the engine. Drive at a safe speed by considering the hill's steepness, length, your vehicle's weight, road conditions, and weather.

questions.question: When stopping, how should you press the brake pedal?

options.text: Press it repeatedly but do not hold it down continuously.
Use the same amount of force every time you slow or stop.

questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal down smoothly and gradually each time you slow or stop. The amount of brake pressure you need depends on how fast you are going and how quickly you need to stop.

questions.question: If oil and water build up in your vehicle's air tanks, what happens to the brakes?
questions.explanation: Drain air tanks daily to remove water and oil. Too much oil and water in the air tanks can prevent your brakes from working properly.

questions.question: If you need to make a quick stop while carrying liquids, what is a safe option?

options.text: Apply the brakes with minimal pressure.

questions.explanation: Vehicles carrying liquids are less stable and may roll over or skid more easily. If you must stop quickly to prevent an accident, the safest methods are the controlled braking method or the stab braking method.
